faqs.question: What is the Xevo G3 QTof used for?
faqs.answer: It's a quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer for both detailed characterization and accurate quantitation, covering challenging small molecules through to complex biotherapeutics on one system.

faqs.question: What mass range does the Xevo G3 QTof cover?
faqs.answer: The calibration range extends to m/z 16,000, which is what brings complex biologics into scope alongside small molecule work.

faqs.question: What is StepWave XS?
faqs.answer: An ion transmission technology that efficiently transmits low mass, labile species, increasing compound coverage and analytical fidelity for analytes that are otherwise easily lost.

faqs.question: What dynamic range does the system offer?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 orders of linear dynamic range for targeted analysis, and up to a 4× increase in in-spectrum dynamic range for untargeted and screening experiments.

faqs.question: What is the difference between linear and in-spectrum dynamic range?
faqs.answer: Linear dynamic range describes the concentration span over which a known analyte quantifies reliably. In-spectrum dynamic range describes how large an abundance difference can be resolved within a single spectrum, which matters when low-abundance components sit alongside high-abundance ones.

faqs.question: Can one instrument really handle both qualitative and quantitative work?
faqs.answer: That's the design intent — Waters positions it as a flexible multifunctional instrument delivering high-quality quantitative and qualitative data sets, maximizing system usage across both workflow types.

faqs.question: What is waters_connect?
faqs.answer: An informatics ecosystem harmonizing workflows across development, manufacturing, and QC, offering compliance-ready workflows with security-controlled access, full data traceability, and networked deployment.

faqs.question: How does the system support the transition from development to QC?
faqs.answer: Biomolecules and processes are characterized on the Xevo G3 QTof first, then transition to dedicated attribute monitoring assays either on the same system or on the BioAccord System with ACQUITY Premier, with waters_connect carrying the workflow.

faqs.question: What software controls the instrument?
faqs.answer: MassLynx for acquiring, analyzing, managing, and sharing nominal and exact mass MS and MS/MS data, and the waters_connect ecosystem for connected, compliance-ready workflows.

faqs.question: How robust is the instrument for high-throughput use?
faqs.answer: Updated ion optics design and optimized ion beam conditioning are engineered specifically to deliver consistent robustness and reproducibility, maintaining performance and productivity over a longer time period.

faqs.question: Which LC systems pair with the Xevo G3 QTof?
faqs.answer: Waters pairs it with ACQUITY Premier in its own materials, and it has been applied with ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS and M-Class in published application work.

faqs.question: Are detailed performance specifications published?
faqs.answer: Waters does not publish a full specification table for this system on the product page. Detailed performance figures are available on request through Inkarp.

An m/z 16,000 calibration range with tailored informatics handles complex biologics; updated ion optics and detection maximize transmission and dynamic range for challenging small molecules. On the quantitative side, core technology updates deliver up to 5 orders of linear dynamic range for targeted analysis, and up to 4× more in-spectrum dynamic range for untargeted screening in complex matrices. The waters_connect ecosystem then carries those workflows from development through manufacturing into QC, with security-controlled access and full data traceability.

faqs.question: What is the Xevo TQ-S cronos used for?
faqs.answer: It's a tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer for routine quantitative LC-MS/MS analysis, applied to food safety, pesticide residues, nitrosamine quantitation in drug products, and other regulated quantitative testing where sample clean-up is part of the workflow.

faqs.question: How reliable is the instrument over a long run?
faqs.answer: A Waters mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections, with peak area RSD of only 3–8%.

faqs.question: How often does the detector need replacing?
faqs.answer: Fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement annually, based on their internal service history data.

faqs.question: What is the mass range and MRM speed?
faqs.answer: 2 to 2048 m/z, at 555 MRM/sec — which is faster than both the Xevo TQ-XS and Xevo TQ Absolute XR, each at 500 MRM/sec.

faqs.question: Where does cronos sit in the Xevo TQ line?
faqs.answer: It's the entry point on sensitivity, rated ★★ on Waters' five-point scale, below TQ-S micro (★★★), TQ-XS (★★★★), and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★). Waters recommends it for accessible routine quantitative analysis with sample clean-up where capital expenditure is limited.

faqs.question: How is cronos different from the Xevo TQ-S micro?
faqs.answer: They share identical dimensions, mass range, MRM speed, StepWave optics, and acquisition modes. TQ-S micro is rated one step higher on sensitivity and adds APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow source compatibility; cronos uniquely adds ACQUITY Arc chromatographic compatibility.

faqs.question: Which ion sources are compatible?
faqs.answer: APCI, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, and UniSpray. Sources can be changed to extend analytical capacity as demands shift.

faqs.question: Which LC systems can it pair with?
faqs.answer: ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, and ACQUITY UPLC M-Class.

faqs.question: What acquisition modes are available?
faqs.answer: Full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and RADAR — simultaneous full scan and MRM in one acquisition.

faqs.question: What is Exception Focused Review?

faqs.question: Are there compatibility restrictions with waters_connect?

body.text: Xevo TQ-S cronos is a tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer from the Xevo family, built around dependable performance with proven ion guide technology maintaining uptime as standard.

Waters recommends it for accessible routine quantitative analysis with sample clean-up, where capital expenditure is limited — the entry point of the Xevo TQ line rather than its sensitivity flagship.

A mycotoxin study in wheat flour, a complex matrix Waters identifies as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation, showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections at only 3–8% RSD for peak areas.
Mass range is 2 to 2048 m/z, matching every other system in the Xevo TQ line.
MRM speed is 555 MRM/sec — higher than both the Xevo TQ-XS and Xevo TQ Absolute XR, which run at 500 MRM/sec.

Ion source transfer optics use StepWave, the same technology found on the TQ-S micro.
Six acquisition modes are supported: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).

Detection uses a low noise, off-axis, long life photomultiplier; Waters' internal service data on tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 shows fewer than 1% require an annual detector replacement.
Five ion sources are compatible: APCI, ASAP, ESCi, ESI, and UniSpray, with ESI as standard.
Chromatographic compatibility covers ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, and ACQUITY UPLC M-Class.
Dimensions are 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm, which Waters describes as 2–3× narrower than most other instruments in its class.
Electrical power consumption is up to 35% lower and heat output up to 35% less than equivalent competitor products.
Two software platforms are available: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with MassLynx security supported.
waters_connect includes Exception Focused Review (XFR), which Waters states can save up to 50% of data review time.
Third-party interfaces include LIMS and the MassLynx SkyLine interface.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.

sections.title: Reliability Across a Full Campaign
sections.tabSummary: The mycotoxin study and detector longevity data

items: Peak sensitivity on a clean standard tells you what an instrument can do once. A quantitative lab needs to know what it does on injection 900, in a matrix that has been depositing residue since injection one.

Waters answered that specifically. A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix they explicitly name as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — ran 1,000 injections across 5 days of continuous use.
Peak area RSD held between 3 and 8% across that campaign, meaning the instrument's response didn't drift meaningfully as the source accumulated matrix.
Proven ion guide technology is what Waters credits for maintaining uptime as standard, and the Xevo family's inherent robustness is the design lineage behind it.

The detector data carries real provenance rather than being a general claim: fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement on an annual basis, from their own service history.

A low noise, off-axis photomultiplier is the design choice behind that longevity — off-axis geometry keeps neutrals and photons off the detector surface, which is what shortens detector life on in-line designs.

For a lab running regulated routine work, that reliability is what makes the difference between a scheduled maintenance visit and an unplanned investigation into why last week's data doesn't match this week's.

groups.title: Software Flexibility and Review Time
items: Acquisition time is only part of a quantitative workflow's cost. Data review is where analyst hours actually accumulate, particularly in regulated environments where every result needs looking at.
Two software platforms are available, and the choice is real rather than a legacy-versus-current split: waters_connect for Quantitation, and MassLynx v4.2.
waters_connect is a modern, app-based platform delivering efficiency and usability benefits, with Exception Focused Review (XFR) as its distinguishing capability.
XFR surfaces the results that need attention rather than requiring every chromatogram to be reviewed equally — Waters states it can save up to 50% of data review time.
MassLynx v4.2 delivers superior versatility and flexibility across all application areas, and remains the right choice where a lab's methods, training, and validation are established on it.
MassLynx security is supported, and both LIMS and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces are available for connecting into a wider informatics estate.
One important constraint: ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, and ESCi are not available with waters_connect, so the software choice can restrict the inlet and source options.

groups.summary: Changing ionization and chromatography as demands shift
items: An instrument locked to one ionization source is locked to one class of analyte, and analytical demands rarely stay still long enough for that to be safe.
ESI ships as standard, being the most commonly used atmospheric pressure ionization source across routine quantitative work.
Four further sources are compatible — APCI, ASAP, ESCi, and UniSpray — so ionization can be changed to extend analytical capacity as demands shift.
UniSpray is worth specific attention: Waters shows UPLC/MRM data where it improved sensitivity for three compounds that would typically require a change in ionization technique for optimal analysis.
Chromatographic inlets are similarly changeable, spanning ACQUITY Arc, ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, and ACQUITY UPLC M-Class.
That inlet range covers HPLC-compatible work through to microscale separations on the same mass spectrometer, which matters when one instrument serves several method types.
Six acquisition modes add a further dimension of flexibility, with RADAR running full scan and MRM simultaneously so screening and quantitation happen in one injection rather than two.
The waters_connect availability constraint applies here too — several inlets and sources are MassLynx-only, so flexibility and software choice interact.

faqs.question: What is the Xevo TQ-S micro used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer for routine quantitative LC-MS/MS, applied across food testing, PFAS and environmental analysis, clinical research, cannabis testing, and pharmaceutical quantitation.

faqs.question: How often will the instrument need unplanned service?
faqs.answer: Waters' internal global service data shows customers on average need no unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after. Planned scheduled Performance Maintenance visits are still recommended for trouble-free operation.

faqs.question: How reliable is performance over a long campaign?
faqs.answer: A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections, with peak area RSD of 5–9%.

faqs.question: How is Xevo TQ-S micro different from the Xevo TQ-S cronos?
faqs.answer: They share identical dimensions, mass range, MRM speed, StepWave optics, acquisition modes, and detector. TQ-S micro rates one step higher on sensitivity (★★★ versus ★★) and adds APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow ion sources plus APGC chromatographic compatibility. cronos uniquely adds ACQUITY Arc compatibility.

faqs.question: What is the mass range and MRM speed?
faqs.answer: 2 to 2048 m/z, at 555 MRM/sec — matching cronos and faster than both TQ-XS and TQ Absolute XR, each at 500 MRM/sec.

faqs.question: Where does TQ-S micro sit in the Xevo TQ line?
faqs.answer: Second on sensitivity, rated ★★★ on Waters' five-point scale, above cronos (★★) and below TQ-XS (★★★★) and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★).

faqs.question: Which ion sources are compatible?
faqs.answer: APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, ionKey, nanoflow, and UniSpray.

faqs.question: Can the instrument do GC-MS work?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Atmospheric Pressure GC (APGC) source is a field upgrade that extends the platform to AP GC-MS, bringing GC-amenable compounds onto the same mass spectrometer.

faqs.question: Which LC systems can it pair with?
faqs.answer: ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.

faqs.question: What acquisition modes are available?
faqs.answer: Full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, MRM, and RADAR — simultaneous full scan and MRM in one acquisition.

faqs.question: What software options are available?
faqs.answer: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with LIMS and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces and MassLynx security supported.

faqs.question: Are there compatibility restrictions with waters_connect?
faqs.answer: Yes. ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, ESCi, ionKey, and nanoflow are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect, so confirm the source and inlet combination against the software choice.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the instrument need?

faqs.question: What are the power and heat requirements?

faqs.question: How often does the detector need replacing?

body.text: Xevo TQ-S micro is a compact tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer from the inherently robust Xevo family, providing superior performance per square inch alongside exceptional analytical flexibility.
Waters positions it as a laboratory workhorse, offering best value performance per square inch of bench space with unrivalled flexibility to meet changing, growing, or unexpected analytical demands.

Waters' internal global service data shows customers using the instrument will on average not need an unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after — with planned scheduled Performance Maintenance visits still recommended for trouble-free operation.

A mycotoxin study in wheat flour, a complex matrix Waters identifies as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation, showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections at 5–9% RSD for peak areas.
Sensitivity is rated ★★★ on Waters' five-point scale — above Xevo TQ-S cronos (★★), below TQ-XS (★★★★) and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★).
Mass range is 2 to 2048 m/z, and MRM speed is 555 MRM/sec, matching cronos and exceeding both TQ-XS and TQ Absolute XR at 500 MRM/sec.
Ion source transfer optics use StepWave, the same as cronos.
Eight ion sources are compatible: APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, ionKey, nanoflow, and UniSpray — three more than cronos, adding APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow.
Six acquisition modes are supported: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, MRM, and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).
Detection uses a low noise, off-axis, long life photomultiplier; fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 require an annual detector replacement.
Chromatographic compatibility covers ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.
Dimensions are 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm — identical to cronos, and 2–3× narrower than other instruments in its class.
Electricity consumption and associated heat production are up to 34% lower than other instruments in its class.
Two software platforms are available: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with MassLynx security supported.
waters_connect includes Exception Focused Review (XFR), which Waters states can save up to 50% of data review time.
Third-party interfaces include LIMS and the MassLynx SkyLine interface.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.
Note that ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, ESCi, ionKey, and nanoflow are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect.

sections.tabSummary: The service data and the mycotoxin study together

items: Instrument downtime in a quantitative lab is rarely just the repair. It's the requalification afterwards, the backlog that built during it, and the questions about whether data either side of the fault is comparable.

Waters makes a specific, checkable claim: customers using the Xevo TQ-S micro will on average not need an unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after, sourced to their internal global service data on unplanned visits.

Their own caveat travels with it and matters — planned visits for regular scheduled Performance Maintenance are recommended to ensure trouble-free operation. The claim is about unplanned interruptions, not maintenance-free running.
Performance under matrix load is separately evidenced. The mycotoxin study in wheat flour ran 1,000 injections across 5 days of continuous use, holding peak area RSD between 5 and 9%.

Worth noting for anyone comparing directly: Xevo TQ-S cronos returned 3–8% RSD on the equivalent study. TQ-S micro's advantage over cronos sits in sensitivity, source range, and this uptime record rather than in campaign precision.
Detector longevity carries the same provenance as across the Xevo TQ line — fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 require an annual detector replacement.
The off-axis photomultiplier geometry is the design reason: keeping neutrals and photons off the detector surface is what extends life relative to in-line arrangements.

items: Analytical demands change — new regulations, new client requirements, new compound classes — and an instrument locked to one ionization technique ages faster than the science does.
Eight ion sources are compatible: APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, ionKey, nanoflow, and UniSpray.
Three of those are unavailable on the entry-level cronos: APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow. That's the practical capability gap between the two systems beyond sensitivity.

APGC is the significant one. The Atmospheric Pressure GC source is a field upgrade that extends the platform to AP GC-MS, bringing GC-amenable compounds onto the same mass spectrometer rather than requiring a separate instrument.
ionKey and nanoflow open microscale and low-flow work, relevant where sample material is limited or sensitivity needs the concentration advantage that low flow provides.
UniSpray is worth noting: Waters shows UPLC/MRM data where it improved sensitivity for three compounds that would typically require a change in ionization technique for optimal analysis.
Chromatographic inlets are similarly changeable across ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.

The waters_connect constraint applies here as it does across the line — UPC2, UPLC M-Class, ASAP, ESCi, ionKey, and nanoflow are MassLynx-only, so source flexibility and software choice interact directly.

It's what Waters' global service data shows customers using the Xevo TQ-S micro actually experience on average — through the warranty period and for three years beyond it. Scheduled Performance Maintenance still applies, but the unplanned call-out that stops a run mid-campaign is the exception rather than the pattern.

Reliability under load backs it up. A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix Waters names outright as one that contaminates LC-MS instrumentation — ran 1,000 injections across five days of continuous use at 5–9% peak area RSD.

What makes it a workhorse rather than just a dependable box is the range packed into 35.6 cm of bench. Rated one step above the cronos on sensitivity while occupying identical space, with APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow sources available alongside the standard five, and 555 MRM/sec for large panels. Waters calls it best value performance per square inch, and the specification supports the claim.

body.text: Coupled with ACQUITY UPLC, Xevo TQ-XS is built for routine quantitative workflows that need superior sensitivity, adaptability, and flexibility as analytical demands evolve.

StepWave XS ion source transfer optics sit specifically at this tier, positioned between the standard StepWave design on the TQ-S cronos and TQ-S micro, and the StepWave XR optics used on TQ Absolute XR.
Mass range covers 2 to 2048 m/z, with MRM speed reaching 500 transitions per second, supported by a low-noise, off-axis, long-life photomultiplier detector.
Six acquisition modes are available: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).

Ion source compatibility spans APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI, ionKey, Nanoflow, and UniSpray, matched to a chromatographic configuration compatibility list including ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.
In a direct vancomycin comparison, average analyte area counts on Xevo TQ-XS came in more than 10 times higher than on Xevo TQ-S.
A representative liraglutide LLOQ chromatogram at 0.5 ng/mL, extracted from plasma, demonstrates the sensitivity and selectivity available at this tier.

Detector reliability runs high across the installed base, with less than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers requiring a detector replacement annually, based on internal service data from units launched between 2006 and 2022.
Software options include MassLynx v4.2 and waters_connect for Quantitation, both supporting LIMS interfaces and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces, with MassLynx security included as standard.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.

body: What the vancomycin and liraglutide performance data actually demonstrate on Xevo TQ-XS.
A sensitivity claim means more with a direct comparison behind it than a general performance statement alone.

For vancomycin, average analyte area counts on Xevo TQ-XS measured more than 10 times higher than on Xevo TQ-S, a direct, quantified sensitivity gain rather than an approximate improvement. On the low-concentration end, a representative liraglutide LLOQ chromatogram at 0.5 ng/mL, extracted from plasma, shows both the sensitivity and the selectivity available at this concentration, relevant for bioanalytical work operating near a method's detection limit. Behind both results sits the StepWave XS ion source transfer optics, purpose-built for this sensitivity tier within the Xevo TQ family, positioned above the standard StepWave design and below the StepWave XR optics on TQ Absolute XR.

Regulatory approval marks, CE, CB, NRTL, and RCM, round out the instrument's readiness for regulated laboratory environments across multiple regions.
